title: Pushbutton lights a lamp
summary: Your first PLC program: a pushbutton switches a lamp, and a selector switch shows its position on a second lamp.
objectives: Read a digital input and write a digital output
See the input image and the output image in one scan
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    Button1 : BOOL; (* Pushbutton S1, normally open. *)
    Button2 : BOOL; (* Pushbutton S2, normally open. *)
    AutoMode : BOOL; (* Selector S3 in position AUTO. *)
    PartPresent : BOOL; (* Proximity sensor B1 detects a part. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    Lamp1 : BOOL; (* Green lamp H1. *)
    Lamp2 : BOOL; (* Amber lamp H2. *)
    Lamp3 : BOOL; (* Red lamp H3. *)
END_VAR

(* Lamp1 must be on while Button1 is pressed. Lamp2 must show the AUTO position of the selector. *)

END_PROGRAM
instructions: Lamp1 is on exactly while Button1 is pressed.
Lamp2 is on while the selector S3 is in AUTO.
Load the program with Build & Load, then press S1 in the Process view and watch the cause-and-effect panel.
hints: An assignment copies a value: Lamp1 := Button1;
Every scan reads all inputs first, so the lamp follows the button one scan later.

scenarios.title: Press and release S1, then select AUTO

criteria.title: Lamp1 follows the pressed button
criteria.onFail: Lamp1 did not switch on while Button1 was TRUE.

criteria.title: Lamp1 goes off after release
criteria.onFail: Lamp1 stayed on after the button was released.

criteria.title: Lamp2 shows AUTO
criteria.onFail: Lamp2 was off with the selector in AUTO.
